analysis: This PR is documentation only: a new changelog entry, a hardware-support.md note, and an inference.md change that arrived as metadata only. No patch text was supplied for inference.md, so it is a coverage limit; the next pass should check it for prefix-cache or Super-owner statements. The changelog describes unregistered, opt-in, default-off Nemotron Super features: a local HTTP hook with existing auth and 429 busy handling, MTP speculation, batched decode, chunked prefill, an image decoder, and DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE_MEMORY=1. The last of these is a resident recurrent checkpoint bank reserved from load to retirement (changelog line 57). That contradicts T-041's assumption that production has no RAM prefix-cache tier, and contradicts hardware-support.md's "ramPrefix always 0" statement. Cache scoping (cacheSalt), kill-switch behaviour and cross-request reuse of the bank are unspecified. See findings. hardware-support.md lines 13-18 say the Super builder requires a live pending LOAD lease and keeps the fixed-workspace concurrency floor, which is consistent with the process-memory-ledger invariants and no regression. No changes to attestation, App Attest, the coordinator WebSocket, encryption, or billing were visible. The source code was not supplied, so the next pass should verify the prefix-cache scoping and the decoder bounds against the actual implementation.

findings.detail: The changelog adds DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE_MEMORY=1. It opts the Super owner into a resident, RAM-based recurrent checkpoint bank (min(1 GiB, grant/8)) that is reserved from load to retirement and reused across requests. T-041 and its mitigations assume the SSD tier is the sole production cache and that production never constructs or funds a resident-RAM prefix cache. hardware-support.md still says "ramPrefix is always 0 in production". The changelog does not say that reuse is bound to the coordinator-authored cacheSalt (account, model build, prompt contract). It also does not say whether the RAM bank honours the DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE=0 kill switch, which the changelog does not mention. If the bank is not salt-scoped, a malicious consumer could confirm another tenant's prefix through a TTFT hit/miss oracle, or restored state could cross account boundaries. This would be a regression beyond the accepted same-account SEC-035 risk. Fix: update T-041 and the mitigations to cover this tier. State that the bank folds cacheSalt into its lookup key, honours the kill switch, and has no cross-account reuse. Keep the flag off for multi-tenant serving until that is verified.
findings.title: Opt-in resident RAM prefix cache contradicts T-041's "no production RAM tier" assumption and does not say how it is scoped

findings.detail: The opt-in Super owner hook decodes untrusted, consumer-supplied inline PNG/JPEG on the provider with a CPU decoder and ImageIO. It also applies EXIF/XMP orientation and runs a tower and projector pass sized to the largest image. The changelog says geometry is bounded before allocation, but this is a new parser and memory-exhaustion surface (decompression bombs, malformed metadata) inside the process that holds decrypted prompts and the X25519 key. TB-007, T-010 and T-029 do not cover it. The feature is unregistered and default-off, which limits current exposure. Fix: document the parser bounds (pixel count, metadata size, decode time) and add the surface to TB-007. Add fuzz or negative tests before the hook is enabled or registered.
findings.title: New native image-decoding surface for consumer-supplied media is not covered by the threat model
